analysis.title: Global Market Intelligence: October 2026 Recap
key_insights: October saw a global tech/AI unwind: MSCI ACWI -1.7%, Developed Markets -0.8%, Emerging Markets -8.1%. Tech drove global weakness and EM underperformed on Asia Tech and LatAm (Brazil election).

AI sentiment soured on infrastructure spend and capex concerns as elevated yields created funding challenges. Capital was the key bottleneck, and neoclouds were among the main casualties after CDS spreads spiked.
Q3 earnings did not support the AI sector, raising questions about AI monetization amid increasingly negative free cash flow at the hosting layer.
US equities: SPX -0.9%, NDX -6.7%, RTY +0.5%. Mag7 fell 7% after disappointing Q3 earnings and still-elevated spending plans. S&P Equal-Weight rose 4.9%.
Thematic moves in the US: Semis -18%, Memory -26%, AI Positive Sentiment -11.5%, Data Centers -8.2%, Neoclouds -35.3% after CoreWeave CDS moves sparked a broader equity selloff.

Momentum unwound (-7.9% globally) with shorts squeezing. Defensives (+9.6%) outperformed Cyclicals (-13.4%) in the US. Broadening (SPW vs SPX, EU vs US) returned but felt technical rather than fundamental.

Positioning: global hedge fund net returns were about -4% in October with declines in all regions, despite broad indices being flat to up. The US Tactical Positioning Monitor fell to the 33rd percentile as of Oct 29. EU positioning hit the 5th percentile before rebounding to the 14th.
Rates regained safe-haven status despite hot US macro data. US 2Y fell 30bps and 10Y fell 36bps. UST yields became positively correlated with NDX, a flight-to-quality pattern.

The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% with two dissents in favor of a hike. Research said Chair Warsh did not clearly explain the decision to hold, and markets read the press conference as softer than the tightening-biased statement. Research still expects a December hike.

US data: Q3 real GDP +3.4% annualized, October all-industry PMI 57.6, September core PCE +0.32% m/m (3.1% y/y). September payrolls rose only 29k vs 90k consensus, with net downward revisions of 60k and unemployment at 4.2%.

Q3 earnings: SPX EPS growth is 19% y/y with Tech, Industrials and Energy the biggest drivers. SXXP EPS growth is 35% y/y (17% ex-Energy), with 8 of the remaining 10 sectors posting double-digit growth. A weaker euro helped European sales beats.

Europe: SXXP +1.9%, SX5E -2.2%. European banks (SX7E) fell 11.8% on EGB spread widening, with Spain -4% and Italy -3.6%. Defensives outperformed by 8.2%. Euro area CPI rose to 3.8% y/y and research raised its EA headline forecast to 4.0%.

France: budget negotiations, protests and fiscal concerns drove OAT underperformance and wider intra-EMU spreads. Part of the widening reversed late in the month after Moody's did not downgrade France.

Asia: MXAP -6.1%. Korea -15.4%, Taiwan -8.3%, Japan -4.1%, China -7.0%, Star50 -24.1%. Foreign selling reached $15bn in Korea and $32bn in Taiwan. Australia (+3.7%) and India (+1.4%) held up on low AI exposure.

FX and commodities: DXY +0.4%, EM FX -0.6%, BRL down over 5% after Lula's surprise runoff win. EUR is the most short currency across JPM FX strategists' metrics. Energy +7.6% on Middle East tensions, gold -6.8%, silver -18.7%.
Research expects hikes from the ECB in December and March, from the BoE in November, and from the BoJ in December. The BoJ held at 1.25% in October.
US midterms: a soft blue wave is priced in, while a big blue wave could be a risk for Tech. Focus is on Texas.

sector_views.rationale: Tech and AI were the key drivers of October weakness on capex and funding concerns, with Semis -18% and Neoclouds -35.3%. This is a description of the month's performance, not a formal sector rating.
Defensives outperformed Cyclicals by a wide margin in the US (+9.6% vs -13.4%) and by 8.2% in Europe, led by Healthcare and Staples. This describes performance, not a formal rating.
SX7E fell 11.8% on EGB spread widening, with UK Banks down 13.4%. This describes performance, not a formal rating.

earnings_insights: Q3 SPX EPS growth is 19% y/y (as reported by JPM Market Intelligence, already reported). The EPS surprise was 3 percentage points in the US and 13 percentage points in Europe, but the share of companies beating estimates is lower than last quarter.
Q3 SXXP EPS growth is 35% y/y (already reported), or 17% ex-Energy. 8 of the remaining 10 sectors posted double-digit earnings growth.
Mag7 fell 7% in October after disappointing Q3 earnings and still-elevated spending plans.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Broadly in line with expectations. Private domestic demand rose 4.9% on strong consumer spending and business investment.
The October PMI of 57.6 implies about 5% annualized growth, so there is upside risk to this forecast.
Suggests resilient activity, though signals for 4Q are mixed.
Hiring softened. The prior two months were revised down by a net 60k.
The Fed held with two dissents in favor of a hike. Research expects a December hike.
Consistent with research's 1.5% annualized 4Q forecast. Germany 52.8, France 48.4.
Research raised its EA headline inflation forecast to 4.0% y/y, largely on energy. Core is expected to stay broadly stable at 2.55%.
Led lower by weaker consumer and retail confidence.
Research lifted its forecast for a peak near 4.6% in 1Q27 as energy costs feed through.
Payroll employment resumed growth, a tentative labour-market improvement.
After +0.4% in both June and July. Research expects growth to slow toward 1% from 4Q as energy bills weigh on real incomes.
Held, viewed as a hawkish pause. Research expects a December hike.

risk_factors: AI funding: elevated yields, neocloud financing stress (CDS spikes) and heavy hyperscaler capex, with investors questioning their willingness to absorb further supply.
Negative free cash flow at the AI hosting layer and unproven AI monetization.
France fiscal and political uncertainty, with continued intra-EMU spread pressure.
Brazil fiscal uncertainty after the election outcome.
Middle East escalation pushing energy prices higher and feeding inflation.
A big blue wave in the US midterms could be a risk for Tech.
Sticky inflation with softening hiring, and a Fed that held despite a tightening bias.
vol_and_positioning: Global HF net returns were down about 4% in October with declines in all regions, even as broad US and European indices were flat to up.
US Tactical Positioning Monitor fell to the 33rd percentile as of Oct 29, with a neutral 4-week change. EU positioning hit the 5th percentile before rebounding to the 14th.
The momentum unwind came with short squeezes. Global momentum fell 7.9%, with European MOMO down 14.5%. European MOMO shorts rallied, including Chemicals (+4.9%) and Defence (+8%).
UST yields became positively correlated with NDX. High-yield spreads briefly revisited their 2026 wides, and the pace of investment-grade spread widening slowed late in the month.
EUR screens as the most short currency across JPM FX strategists' metrics.
geopolitical: Renewed Middle East flare-ups, including tensions between Houthis and Saudi Arabia, drove oil higher in October.
UK budget was a 'do no harm' budget with muted market reaction. The bank surcharge came in below consensus expectations.
France: budget negotiations, protests and fiscal-credibility concerns widened intra-EMU spreads. Moody's did not downgrade France and protests calmed late in the month.
US midterms: a soft blue wave is priced in, while a big blue wave could be a risk for Tech. Focus on Texas.
Brazil: Lula's surprise runoff victory after trailing Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round reversed the election-driven rally. Equities, BRL and rates came under pressure on fiscal uncertainty.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 earnings were positive in aggregate, with SPX EPS growth at 19% y/y and Tech among the biggest contributors. Medium-term demand support remains in AI demand and corporate earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Capital is the key bottleneck. Neocloud CDS spreads spiked, hosting-layer free cash flow is increasingly negative, and investors question how much more hyperscaler and neocloud supply they will absorb.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 GDP grew 3.4% and the October all-industry PMI of 57.6 implies upside risk to the 1.75% Q4 forecast.
tension_points.bear_case: Consumer-spending momentum slowed late in Q3 and September payrolls rose just 29k. Rates rallied despite hot data, which points to flight-to-quality demand.
